newsitem.title: USA: Enron, PGE court Ore. community groups.
newsitem.headline: Enron, PGE court Ore. community groups.

text.p: Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co said Monday twelve community service and public interest organizations support the companies' merger plans based on long-term commitments to public programs.
As part of the agreement, if the merger is completed, Portland General (PGE) and Enron will each contribute $10 million to the PGE Foundation, to be used in Oregon.
Portland General Corp, parent of PGE, and Enron, a Houston-based energy company, are seeking approval to merge from the Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC).

Last week, the companies reached an agreement with 13 environmental and public interest groups, under which the groups pledged support of the merger in return for financial and other commitments to environmental and competitive initiatives.
The staff of the OPUC last week recommended approval of the merger, but said certain conditions, including a substantial multi-year customer rate cut, need to be met.
The OPUC will begin a three-day conference on the merger plans Wednesday and is scheduled to make its decision March 17.

Enron and PGE said the latest groups to enodorse the merger were: the John Inskeep Environmental Learning Center, Friends of Trees, Wolftree Ecological Education, Jackson Bottom Preserve, Stop Oregon Litter and Vandalism, Friends of Mt. Scott and Kellogg Creeks Watershed, Association of Northwest Steelheaders, Environmental Federation of Oregon, Metro Parks and Greenspaces, Portland Audubon Society, The Wetlands Conservancy and Friends of Smith and Bybee Lakes.
